report.summary: Chunk 5 of 7: evaluate_change, verify_before_state, corpus load/save/run, and seed helpers. Key claim 'never raises' is broken due to unhandled KeyError. Other claims about ordering and frozen selection are kept.
risks: evaluate_change lines 1159,1161 | critical | Unhandled KeyError on missing task keys contradicts 'never raises' docstring | Add try-except or guard with .get()
_changed_files line 1320 | medium | git diff with sha^ fails for initial commit | Handle initial commit case
_blob line 1328 | low | Returns None on failure, caller may not handle | Ensure callers check for None
todos: Fix evaluate_change to handle missing task keys (e.g., 'repo', 'base_revision') to truly never raise.

claims.text: The whole measurement happens in ONE disposable worktree, in this order: FREEZE the selection -> checkout base -> overlay tests -> RUN BEFORE -> judge the TASK -> apply the change -> RUN AFTER -> judge the CHANGE
claims.why: The code follows this order: freeze_selection (line 1172), disposable_worktree (line 1174), apply_test_overlay (line 1177), _run_lists (line 1181), judge_before_state (line 1185), apply_patch (line 1205), _run_lists (line 1210), judge_after_state (line 1216).

claims.text: The selection is frozen FIRST, before the worktree exists and long before any candidate bytes are applied
claims.why: freeze_selection is called at line 1172 before disposable_worktree at line 1174.

claims.text: the after-state is run against that same frozen object -- so the thing being measured cannot be influenced by the thing being measured.
claims.why: The same `selection` object is used for both before (line 1181) and after (line 1210) runs.

claims.text: The before-state is measured every time, in the same tree the after-state is measured in. It is never read from a stored receipt here
claims.why: The before-state is measured by _run_lists and judge_before_state in the same worktree; no receipt loading code exists in this function.

claims.text: use_reference evaluates the task's OWN fix commit (reference_revision) instead of a candidate patch.
claims.why: When use_reference is True, change_bytes is set via reference_patch at line 1199; otherwise patch_bytes is used.

claims.text: a task whose own reference patch does not produce fixed is not a task.
claims.why: This claim about corpus validation is not enforced in this chunk; it is a policy stated elsewhere.

The function uses bare `except Exception` on line 1211, but `task['repo']` on line 1159 can raise KeyError if 'repo' is missing, and `task['base_revision']` on line 1161 can raise KeyError. These are not caught by the except clause because they occur before the try block begins at line 1173.

claims.text: The frozen declaration and its digest travel on the result.
claims.why: The CorrectnessResult is constructed with `selection=selection` on line 1133 and also via `finish` calls.

claims.text: Used when seeding a corpus. A candidate task that does not survive this is reported, with its reasons, and not admitted -- which is the measurement that says how much a corpus is worth.
claims.why: This chunk does not contain the seeding logic that consumes verify_before_state.

claims.text: Read the corpus, or [] if it does not exist yet. Sorted by id.
claims.why: If path does not exist returns [] (line 1256); returns sorted data (line 1259).

claims.text: Overwrite the corpus. Deterministic formatting, same contract as harness.write_baseline / mint.save_minted_tasks.
claims.why: The claim about matching contract of other functions cannot be verified from this chunk alone.

claims.text: Evaluate every task against its OWN reference patch. The corpus's own gate.
claims.why: The function calls evaluate_change with use_reference=True for each task (line 1294).

claims.text: the corpus validating ITSELF: a task whose reference fix does not produce fixed is not a task, and an evaluator that cannot show that its corpus discriminates is in the same position as the pytest gate it exists to strengthen.
claims.why: The function returns a 'discriminates' field (line 1308) that is true only if all tasks have outcome FIXED.

claims.text: Counts are reported per outcome and NEVER blended into a single 'score' -- task_invalid and could_not_run in particular are not failures of the change, and folding them into one number would hide exactly the distinction this module was built for.
claims.why: The function returns a 'counts' dict per outcome (line 1303) and a 'per_task' list with individual outcomes (line 1310), no single score is computed.

claims.text: Seeded from this repo's own fix commits with --seed; every task's lists were MEASURED (run on the base revision, then again under the commit's own fix), never taken from the diff on trust.
claims.why: This chunk does not contain the seeding logic; it only contains _changed_files, _blob, _test_functions which are helpers for seeding.

claims.text: 'before_state' is the receipt of that measurement and 'selection_digest' freezes what was declared -- the gate refuses a task whose lists no longer digest to it.
claims.why: The gate logic is not present in this chunk.

claims.text: 'dropped_candidates' records every node that did not survive, and why.
Verify with 'python -m daedalus.eval.correctness --verify'; re-measure every task against its own reference fix with '--run'.
claims.why: CLI entry points are not in this chunk.

claims.text: These tasks are NOT in harness.all_tasks(): slice recall cannot grade them (they have no must_include and would score a vacuous 1.0), and the harness refuses them.

observations.what: evaluate_change can raise unhandled KeyError when task lacks 'repo' or 'base_revision' keys, contradicting the 'never raises' claim.
The _changed_files function runs 'git diff' with the parent revision sha^; this may fail for the initial commit (no parent).
_blob function uses 'git show' without error handling for missing revisions; returns None on failure, but the caller may not handle None gracefully.
